lines.en: Later that day...in a room so quiet we could hear each other’s hearts beat.
It didn’t take long for Noriko to find us a safehouse of sorts — just a quick conversation with the woman at the front desk who handed her a room key, no questions asked.
It makes me a little jealous, if I’m being honest. How she can just use her role to get the things she wants and then hand them over to me like it’s no trouble at all.
I probably shouldn’t feel that way given the things I have taken when I wore her shoes, but I do.
And I’d go as far as saying it brings back bad memories if all of my memories weren’t already somewhat tainted to begin with.
Regardless, here we are — bathed in ambient silence disrupted only by conversations that, while nostalgic, feel more like informative briefings on my past self than anything else.
We talk of days past and days yet to come.
Noriko embellishes each anecdote with unimportant details that walk the fine line between just existing for imagery and existing to try and help me remember something.
And it works. It works in both regards.
I can remember more of the past now that the largest gaps in time have been filled in by those I’ve loved and either lost or am losing.
Yet those pivotal, formative memories that clog my hippocampus like red hair swallowed by the drain disrupt my train of thought when the roots they take sprawl out onto my one-track mind.
In taking root, however, I can feel things start to fall into place.
I can feel them reaching out and strangling things I’ve subconsciously suppressed, integrating them once more into a network of thoughts and feelings reminiscent of how trees talk to one another.
So sit in my shade and listen to the sounds of a nearby station calling out where we are or where we’re headed.
There’s only a stop or two left after this one.
And if you miss your train, you might have to spend the night here.
: Nostalgic, isn’t it? Sitting next to one another in a dimly lit room — hiding from Nee-chan while we talk about whatever crosses our minds.
: If I didn’t know any better, I’d think you might be about to tutor me.
: Frankly speaking, I don’t think there’s much left I can teach you at this point.
: Oh? Is that why you gave up on teaching? Just...ran out of relevant information? Assuming of course that you didn’t run out the first time you left me to fend for myself.
: Two times now you have put my education at risk, Sensei. Two times now, you have pawned me off on someone else and just hoped I’d be able to figure things out on my own.
: Three if you want to count my initial departure. But I don’t think I was tutoring you yet back when I ran away from Niki.
: That’s why I excluded it. It’s important to mention that you didn’t just run away from Niki, though. You ran away from all of us.
: My mom still asks about you all the time. It’s always, “Where’s my son? Where’s Akira? When’s Akira coming to visit?” every time I help out at the restaurant or drop by to say hello.
: I’m surprised she still cares at all after everything I put you guys through.
: I’m not. She probably understood what you were going through better than either of us back then. We were just confused and betrayed.
: But we get it now. And we don’t blame you for it, Onii-chan.
: Niki still blames me for it. She’ll never let me live that down.
: Sure. But Nee-chan only blames you on the surface. Deep down, she understands. That’s why she still loves you so much when, realistically, she could bag any boy or girl in this city.
: That said, I can’t help but feel a little angry that you keep letting me wander off on my own instead of continuing to cultivate my mind in ways only an older brother could.
: By filling it with worry and doubt and any other negative emotion you’d be burdened by receiving from me?
: You always say that, but you’ve been my teacher twice now and have never filled me with worry or doubt either time.
: At least until you started messing around with Maya. I will concede that I may have been worried then.
: But back then, it was mostly just worries about how you were starting to favor her over me. And not so much worrying about what I should have been worrying about.
: Which was...
: How the hell you were managing to fit it inside of that little girl.
: That was...more vulgar and direct than I expected to hear. But yes. That’s exactly what you should have been worried about. But you weren’t.
: So you subjected her to a life of wanting nothing but me and I’m sure I don’t need to inform you how terrible that is.
: You sure don’t...
: Do you regret it, though? Doing those things with Maya? Tutoring? All of it? Is there not a single bright spot to be found in any of those years?
: Sure there is. I have you, don’t I?
: Heheh~ Correct answer, Onii-chan! You’ve learned well from today’s marathon of sibling love. The time has clearly come for me to begin tutoring you instead.
: It’s been a good day...yeah.
: Mm...it must be if it can do...whatever that is to your face.
: I think kids these days are calling it a “smile,” but you’d know more about that than me.
: I don’t know, Onii-chan. You’re pretty clearly the one more experienced with kids between the two of us.
: Okay. Smile gone. And remind me to never try to do that in front of you again.
: Now why would I do that? It’s a little sister’s sole mission in life to make her big brother smile, isn’t it? Otherwise, he won’t want to protect her from potential evil suitors.
: I’m too nice to face all those evil suitors on my own, Onii-chan. I need you to reject them for me. And beat them up if they try to get too handsy.
: Just maybe not too badly or you’ll wind up having to spend your days with Uta’s brother instead of an idol, a bunch of MILFs, and an entire high school.
: Is it just me, or is that bright spot I referenced earlier starting to get a little dim?
: Hey! I take great pride in being your bright spot! And if anything, you’re super lucky I’m still glowing after all these years!
: If anything, you’re lucky it wasn’t you in Maya’s shoes back then. Because I imagine our relationship now would be a lot different if you were.
: You mean like if you touched me and stuff instead?
: Yes. But not if you’re going to say something like “I wish you did” or any of those other things I know you only say to try and appeal to me when you’re clearly better than that.
: I am better than that. And I’m glad it wasn’t me in Maya’s shoes back then because I don’t think I’d be able to look at you the same way I do today.
: Mistakes are harder to forgive when they happen to you.
: They’re still happening, though. And they have happened to you. Do I need to remind you of the age gap here? Or have you just forgotten about that like everyone else?
: I actually think it’s more of a split between those who “forget” about it and those who lean into it because they think it’s hot.
: You forgive me either way, though. And that’s because you’re caught in the web as well.
: I do forgive you and I am caught in the web, yes. But that has nothing to do with why I forgive you.
: Then...why? What else would just let you keep overlooking mistakes like the ones I’ve made? Because you’re not stupid. And I know you’re impulsive, but-
: Because we’re family, silly.
: And no matter what happens, you’ll always be my brother first and a man second.
: But...
: Why...do you still so relentlessly pursue me then?
: One does not choose to be a brocon. One is simply born that way.
: Noriko-
: Don’t “Noriko” me. I’ve been nothing but gleefully platonic all day long and I’m not about to get scolded for a bunch of stuff I’ve said or done in the past.
: If you want me to be your sister and nothing else, that’s what I’ll be. And I’ll be happy doing it because, again, I love you like you share my blood.
: And that’s probably not the most appropriate or...normal way to word that, but it’s the truth. You are my brother.
: And every single time I get to look at you and say “Onii-chan,” it’s like there’s a surge of energy coursing through me that makes me feel like I can do anything.
: And with you by my side, I think I can. That’s why I’m still in the background of my fantasies. That’s why I can forgive you for all the “mistakes” you make with my friends.
: I love you in ways that only a younger sibling could. And you don’t need to understand it, but-
: Good. Because I don’t understand it.
: And it’s not...just because you also want to fuck me sometimes.
: It’s because I inherently don’t understand why that...familial connection alone would bring you joy when it did nothing but fucking...terrorize me for my entire life.
: Sorry, I...
: It’s just...
: You mention your brother so rarely, I...forgot you even had one.
: Yeah, well...
: That’s why I have a hard time understanding the way you feel about me. And how you can be so happy to have something I was so...
: So...afraid of.
: Afraid?...
: Why?
: He had everything I didn’t. He was everything I’m not.
: And He lorded it over me as if He was God himself.
: He blamed me for what happened to my father. He blamed me for what happened to my mother. And I believed Him.
: I believed Him because I saw what He was and I saw what I was and it was...night and fucking day, Noriko.
: I was weak. He was a man. I was small. He was this...fucking colossus. I can’t even...I don’t...there are no words to explain how different we were.
: He’d lock me in the closet for days at a time. Tear up my clothes. Piss on me. Make me act and...bark like a fucking dog just so I could eat.
: But it was less like being a pet and more just...something to step on. And kick...and beat...and just genuinely fucking terrorize and abuse...
: And I didn’t have anyone to protect me from that.
: At least...not at first.
: But then He met someone.
: A girl.
: With beautiful red hair and a soft, delicate voice — who dressed like a character from an old movie and wrote poetry that could move even the most heartless of monsters.
: She didn’t know I existed at first. But one day, she must have heard me.
: I can still see it...the glare of the sun when she pulled open the door of the closet. Him, towering over her, laughing like He’d forgotten I was in there.
: She looked at me...and her eyes immediately doubled in size. But before I could pull the door shut, she...
: She turned around and slapped Him so hard that, for the first time in my life, I got to see Him on the receiving end of physical pain.
: “How long has he been in there?!” she asked Him. And I can’t remember how He replied, but...
: The next thing I knew, she was pulling me out. And crying on my behalf while I just...stood there. Sweaty. Covered in piss. Worried I’d get her dress dirty.
: That’s why I can’t stand when people call her a monster. Because she wasn’t.
: She was the first person to ever show me there was more to life than what I had.
: I never slept in the closet again after that. From that point on it was just-
: ...Wait, when did we start holding hands?
: Akira...why?
: Why haven’t you ever told me this?
: I haven’t told anyone. You’re the first.
: But why did you wait so long?...Why did you keep that inside for so many years? Didn’t it hurt? Doesn’t it hurt?
: I mean, He’s dead now. So I got the last laugh in the end.
: What about Ami?...Does she know he put you through all of that? That girl was her mom, right? And she-
: No, and I’d prefer it if she didn’t. So please don’t say anything to her about it. I’m trusting you, Noriko.
: Of course, Onii-chan. But-
: If it’s okay, can we not make a big deal out of this right now? Because it’s starting to feel a lot like the time your sister got me to stop repressing something and that really sucked.
: So Nee-chan...doesn’t know either?
: Nope...just you.
: Why?
: You’ve never put me first before.
: Why now?
: I just...didn’t like that whole “seeing you as more of a brother than a man” thing when both of those words cut pretty deeply in certain contexts. To me, at least.
: Should I not call you my brother anymore then?
: You can call me whatever you want. It’s fine if it’s you.
: But I’d feel more comfortable knowing you just look at me as “me” rather than a brother or a man or...even a teacher.
: I’m Akira. You’re Noriko. That’s it. That’s all it needs to be.
I’m not sure how long we stay like this for.
But I’m pretty sure of where it’ll go if we don’t break apart.
: Noriko, I...
: I don’t know if...we should really be...you know.
: Know what? Say it.
: Say it.
: What shouldn’t we do?
: What don’t you want to do with me?
: And what happens if I want to do it with you?
: It was a mistake telling me to look at you as just “you” Akira.
: When I do that, it suddenly becomes a lot harder to stop myself from acting out on certain things.
: Sure. But what you’re feeling isn’t love or lust right now...it’s pity. You don’t know how to handle being the only person who knows something about me. So your mind is going haywire and-
: Don’t tell me what’s going on in my mind. Not when you can’t even figure out what’s going on with yours.
: Because I can forgive you for keeping all of this inside to protect yourself. And I can forgive you for not wanting to tell anyone now because it’s hard or it hurts or it’s embarrassing.
: Fuck, I can forgive you for almost anything because of who you are and what we have.
: But if you hand me a piece of yourself that I get to keep and I don’t get to give any part of myself to you?...
: How is that fair?
: How is any of this fair?
: And how can you look at me — Noriko — while I look at you as Akira and not find yourself drowning in a lifetime worth of wanting?
: Because you might be perturbed by the thought that I would see you as a man...but I want you to see me as a woman.
: And I want you to love me the way you love. Because if you don’t now, I might never believe you.
: This is exactly how it ended last time and now your sister lives in my house...
: I am not my sister.
: I am my own person who feels and thinks and wants and loves. And I am tired of pushing all of that aside in favor of other people.
: But I will not choose for you. And if you decide that you want a sister and nothing else, all you need to do is stay silent in response to the following haiku.
: A haiku? Now?
: What’s wrong? You like poets, don’t you?
: I mean...that’s not exactly true. It’s just that...it’s easier for me to understand someone’s feelings when they’re conveyed in a way that-
: Then understand this, Akira.
: If you take me here...
: You will have me forever.
: There is no escape.
: That is fine by me.
: I’m sick of running away.
: You’ve suffered enough.
: A haiku...
: It took me a second to think of one. Sorry for the suspense.
: Does this mean...
: It means you’re going to have to stop crying or I won’t be able to go through with this.
: I don’t think I can. All the confidence I had a second ago has now been replaced by nerves. This feels too real. Like I’m...dreaming or something.
: Do your dreams normally begin with me trauma dumping all over you?
: No. But they normally end with you on top of me.
: Then what do you say we make half of a dream come true tonight, Noriko?
: Mhm...
: You realize that by doing this, you’ll effectively be committing incest, right?
: Mhm! Mhm...
: It’s okay if it’s you...Onii-chan.
: Then stop looking so scared...I’ll take good care of you.
: I’m sure you will. Very sure. Just...what if Ami is hiding in the closet or something? I still have PTSD from that.
: Then she takes after me in even more ways than I thought.
: Not funny, Onii-chan. I don’t want this to set a precedent in which you start making self-deprecating trauma jokes around me from now on.
: I wouldn’t worry about that. I don’t think I’ll have much time for jokes at all between everything I want to do to you.
: Oh god...I’m about to cum and we haven’t even started yet.
: Yes we have...
: Aaah! Onii-chan! Or...A..Akira? What do I...uhh...how should I-
: Let’s go with Onii-chan today. You’re at your cutest when you’re being my little sister.
: Which is why I’m already like this.
: Hah! Onii...chan!~ Ah!
